σμύρνα.as:
σμύρνα
(in some MSS, ζμ-; v. Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for מוֹר מֹר ;]
myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: Mt 2:11, Jo 19:39.†

σμυρνίζω.sd: to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic)
σμυρνίζω.as:
*† σμυρνίζω
(< σμύρνα),
1. intrans., to be like myrrh (Diosc., i, 79).
2. Trans., to mingle or drug with myrrh: pass., Mk 15:23.†

Σμύρνα.long: Smyrna, a great port of the Roman province Asia.
Σμύρνα.sd: Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor
Σμύρνα.as:
Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ
Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Re 1:112:8.†

σμαράγδινος.as:
*† σμαράγδινος
(< σμάραγδος, q.v.),
1.of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11).
2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: Re 4:3 (for the construction, v. Swete, in l.; Zorell, s.v.).†

σμάραγδος.sd: the emerald or green gem so called
σμάραγδος.as:
σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ
(and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: Ex 28:9 (שֹׁהַם) 36:17 (39:10) (בָּרֶקֶת), Ez 28:13 (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;]
emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, s.v.; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): Re 21:19.†
